text:
Fixed in `middleware/proxy.go`.

Root cause: when a balancer has no targets, `Next()` panicked — `randomBalancer.Next` called `rand.Intn(0)` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` did `b.i % uint32(0)` (division by zero), so a request through `Proxy(...)` with an empty balancer crashed the server instead of answering.

Changes:
- `randomBalancer.Next` and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` now return `nil` when `len(b.targets) == 0` (round-robin also takes the read lock while inspecting the target slice).
- `ProxyWithConfig` handles a `nil` target from the balancer by returning `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable`, so the client gets a clean `503 Service Unavailable` instead of a panic.

Verified: a request through `Proxy(NewRandomBalancer(nil))` and `Proxy(NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{}))` now yields HTTP 503, `Next` returns nil without panicking, and the middleware returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable`. Full suite (`go test ./...`, plus `-race` on the proxy tests) passes; no pre-existing test was modified.
#1 (proxy balancer with no targets) is fixed and verified: empty balancers no longer panic, and `Proxy` now returns 503 Service Unavailable. Full test suite still green.

#2 (router.go / TestRouterNoRoutablePath) is still being diagnosed: I'm narrowing down the non-routable-path case in `Router.Find` (looking for panics, wrong handler selection or loops when no route matches). ETA ~12 minutes.
#1 (proxy.go / TestProxyBalancerWithNoTargets): fixed and verified. Empty balancers no longer panic; `Proxy` returns 503 Service Unavailable. Full suite green.

#2 (router.go / TestRouterNoRoutablePath): still in progress. Existing suite is green and fuzzing found no panics/loops, so it is a semantic routing bug (a non-routable path being matched). I'm running a differential test against a reference matcher; ETA ~10 min.

#4 (context.go / TestContext_Scheme): in progress. `Context#Scheme()` currently returns whatever is in X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Protocol / X-Url-Scheme without validating it, so invalid values are trusted instead of being ignored; I'm adding validation so invalid values are skipped and it falls back correctly. ETA ~6 min.

#5 (bind.go / TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap): the fix is written, verification pending. `bindData` bound every map value as `v[0]` (a string) regardless of the map's element type, which panics for `map[string][]string` (and for nil maps); it now supports map[string]string, map[string][]string and map[string]interface{} and skips unsupported element types. ETA ~6 min to confirm with tests.
#2 (router.go): still in progress (semantic routing bug; differential testing against a reference matcher is running). ETA ~8 min.
#4 (context.go Scheme): applying the fix now (validate the forwarded scheme headers, ignore invalid values, fall back correctly). ETA ~3 min.
#5 (bind.go bindDataToMap): code fix applied; verifying with tests now. ETA ~3 min.

#7 (group.go / TestMultipleGroupSamePathMiddleware): diagnosing. `Group.Use` registers catch-all `Any("", NotFoundHandler)`/`Any("/*", NotFoundHandler)` routes, so a second group on the same path overwrites the first group's registrations and middleware. ETA ~8 min.

#8 (middleware/compress.go / TestGzipEmpty): diagnosing. An "empty" response currently still emits the 10-byte gzip header while Content-Encoding is stripped, so the body isn't really empty. ETA ~8 min.

#4 (context.go / TestContext_Scheme): fixed. `Context#Scheme()` no longer trusts arbitrary forwarded header values: X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Protocol and X-Url-Scheme are only honoured when they are a valid scheme (http/https), otherwise the next source is consulted and it falls back to "http". Full suite green.

#5 (bind.go / TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap): fixed. `bindData` now supports the limited map destinations properly — map[string]string (first value), map[string][]string (all values), map[string]interface{} (first value) — creates the map when it is nil, and skips unsupported element types instead of panicking. Full suite green.

#7 (group.go / TestMultipleGroupSamePathMiddleware): not fixed yet. Root cause identified: `Group.Use` registers catch-all routes via `g.Any("", NotFoundHandler)` / `g.Any("/*", NotFoundHandler)`, which registers a handler for every HTTP method at the group path, so a second group on the same path overwrites the first group's registrations (its middleware is then never run for unmatched paths, and method-not-allowed handling is suppressed). The fix needs the group's not-found routes to be registered under a dedicated method key rather than every method. ETA ~10 min.

#8 (middleware/compress.go / TestGzipEmpty): not fixed yet. Diagnosis so far: for an "empty" response the middleware strips Content-Encoding but the gzip writer has already emitted the 10-byte gzip header, so the body is not empty (and the response is left with a bogus gzip body). The fix is to make the empty-response path reset the writer to discard before anything is written, so nothing is emitted. ETA ~10 min.
